description: We bridge the gap between digital software and physical systems. Our team is formed by engineering students passionate about coding, electronics, and creating tech solutions from scratch
summary: AGROROBITT is a free, browser-based 3D platform that turns NASA satellite data into clear, field-ready guidance for smallholder farmers. On an interactive Cesium globe, a farmer searches their town or taps their own hectare, then triggers satellite analysis only when they choose — so no mobile data is wasted and nothing is invented. It reads real surface temperature (MODIS), greenery (NDVI), root-zone moisture (SMAP / POWER) and weather forecasts (Open-Meteo), explains them in plain language, warns about drought, frost, heat and waterlogging, and compares three transparent crop-rotation options. It addresses Field Shift by helping farmers adapt to a changing climate with data they can actually understand, while always respecting the true resolution of each satellite and encouraging on-the-ground verification. Fully bilingual (Spanish / English) and built with Next.js, TypeScript and CesiumJS, it runs on low-end phones so precision agriculture can finally reach the people who need it most.
details:
What it does and how it works

AGROROBITT is an accessible 3D web app. A farmer opens it, searches their town (or uses GPS), and navigates a Cesium 3D globe. They outline their own parcel by clicking its corners. Nothing is queried until they press "Analyze this land" — only then do we contact NASA and partner services. The app returns real readings (surface temperature, greenery, root-zone moisture, upcoming rain), paints an honest thermal map of the parcel, and produces preventive alerts with sources and evidence. Finally, it compares three crop-rotation options using transparent rules, and lets the farmer keep a field logbook that fine-tunes those recommendations.

Benefits

- Accessible — no data is consumed while exploring; queries happen only on demand.

- Honest — satellite resolution is shown as-is; gaps from clouds stay empty instead of being filled with fake color.

- Understandable — results are written in plain, neighbor-to-neighbor language, not scientific jargon.

- Bilingual — full Spanish / English interface.

- Portable — runs on low-end phones and browsers.

Intended impact

Bring NASA's climate-adaptation power to underserved smallholder farmers, giving them earlier warnings (drought, frost, heat, waterlogging) and clearer crop decisions for a shifting growing season — so adaptation arrives on time, not late.

Tools, languages, hardware and software

- Languages / frameworks: TypeScript, JavaScript, Next.js (Turbopack), React, Node.js.

- 3D globe: CesiumJS (Cesium Ion world terrain).

- Visualization / output: Recharts (charts), jsPDF (PDF reports), lucide-react (icons).

- Testing: Vitest (unit) and Playwright (browser E2E).

- Data services: NASA GIBS, NASA POWER, NASA AppEEARS, ISRIC SoilGrids, Open-Meteo, Esri basemap.

How it is creative

Instead of upsampling coarse data to look precise, AGROROBITT fuses products of very different resolutions into one honest, hectare-level explanation — keeping each source's real resolution, date and unit. Its transparent "Synthetic Intelligence" layer turns the farmer's own logbook into explainable, rule-based recommendations rather than a black box.

Factors the team considered

Data frugality (low mobile data use), honesty and traceability (no invented data), farmer literacy (plain language, bilingual), and accessibility (works on low-end devices).
